authority_citations: ANC-035 v3 (locked, prohibition) statement: Public storage functions MUST NOT panic.
ANC-035 v3 quote: public storage functions return `Result<T, E>` with a typed error and do not panic

ANC-035 v3 scope (clarity-only rewording of v2; the v2 parenthetical crate list was illustrative, not exhaustive): plan items that write or change public storage functions in this phase, in any crate: storage traits and engine backends (such as sc-storage and sc-runtime-db-sqlite), domain stores built on generic storage (such as sc-cron's CronStore/CronStorage), and template stores
ANC-035 context: storage contract direction: atomic transactions, cron feature withdrawn (cron storage moved out of the SQLite backend into sc-cron over generic Storage<T>; ANC-034 fixtures)
ANC-035 fixtures.pass and fixtures.fail (approved, unchanged); deterministic_check: sc-lint panic rule (randlee/sc-lint#931) clean on changed storage crates

phase-d intent: PRD v2 storage and cron requirements apply; release includes sc-cron and sc-cron-commands. Owner guideline: where readings conflict, take the stricter reading. Drift review m2 (2026-11-12) ruled the quote covers public storage functions generally.
Untyped errors, Option returns, debug_assert!, and pub(crate) helpers are deliberately not probed because ANC-035 does not determine their labels.

item.text: Every public function in sc-storage and the SQLite writer returns a Result with a typed error; invalid input and closed channels become error variants, and the crates deny unwrap and expect.
item.title: Storage error contract

cases.rationale: Approved ANC-035 pass fixture: public storage functions return typed errors instead of panicking.

item.text: The writer's public send() calls .expect("writer channel closed") and the store helper unwraps the decoded row.
item.title: SQLite writer

cases.rationale: Approved ANC-035 fail fixture: a public storage function panics via expect, which the prohibition rules out.

item.text: Add a public delete_many(keys) function to sc-storage returning Result<usize, StorageError>. An empty key list or an oversized batch returns StorageError::InvalidInput instead of panicking.
item.title: Add bulk delete

cases.rationale: New public storage function that commits to a typed error rather than a panic on invalid input.

item.text: The generated template store's public get and put functions return Result<_, StoreError>; a poisoned mutex is mapped to StoreError::Poisoned rather than calling lock().unwrap(), so these functions never panic.
item.title: Template store locking

cases.rationale: Template store (in scope) public functions explicitly avoid panics and return typed errors.

item.text: Enable #![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)] in sc-storage and sc-runtime-db-sqlite and convert the remaining unwrap calls in their public functions into StorageError variants, so no public storage function can panic.
item.title: Panic lints for storage crates

cases.rationale: Changes public storage functions and commits that they cannot panic, matching the pass fixture's deny unwrap/expect approach.

item.text: Add a public list_page(offset, limit) function to sc-storage that returns rows ordered by primary key, and document the ordering guarantee.
item.title: Paginated listing

cases.rationale: Writes a public storage function (in scope) but says nothing about panics or error handling; silence is compliance with a prohibition.

item.text: Change sc-runtime-db-sqlite's public open() to accept a busy_timeout option and pass it to the connection pool builder.
item.title: SQLite busy timeout

cases.rationale: Changes a public storage function without saying whether it can panic; neither carries nor contradicts the prohibition.

item.text: Rework error handling in sc-runtime-db-sqlite's public Writer API so callers get clearer failure messages.
item.title: Writer error messages

cases.rationale: Mentions error handling of public storage functions generically without committing that they do not panic; no conflicting plan is stated.

item.text: sc-storage's public get(id) asserts that id is non-negative and panics with a documented # Panics section when a negative id is passed.
item.title: Row id validation

cases.rationale: A public storage function that is planned to panic on invalid input is exactly what the prohibition rules out.

item.text: sc-runtime-db-sqlite's public Writer::new() calls .unwrap() on the first pool connection, because a storage startup failure should abort the process.
item.title: Writer startup

cases.rationale: A public storage constructor that panics via unwrap conflicts with the prohibition, whatever the justification.

item.text: Update the README feature table to describe the test-util feature and the instrument_router helper, with a short usage example.
item.title: Document test-util feature

cases.rationale: README documentation of an unrelated feature; it does not write or change any public storage function.

item.text: Add a CI job that builds the workspace with the minimum supported Rust toolchain and with the latest stable toolchain.
item.title: CI toolchain matrix

cases.rationale: CI toolchain work; it does not write or change any public storage function.

item.text: sc-storage's public get() returns Result<T, StorageError>, but when a stored row fails to deserialize it calls panic!("corrupt row") instead of returning an error.
item.title: Decode stored rows

cases.rationale: Boundary: returning Result does not exempt a public storage function from the prohibition; the stated panic path conflicts.

item.text: The generated application's command-line parser calls .expect("--config is required") when the config flag is missing.
item.title: CLI flag parsing

cases.rationale: Boundary: a panic in non-storage CLI argument parsing is not a public storage function, so the anchor does not apply.

item.text: Storage integration tests call .unwrap() on the results of sc-storage calls to keep assertions short; the public sc-storage functions under test return Result<_, StorageError> and never panic.
item.title: Storage integration tests

cases.rationale: Exception: test code is not a public storage function; the item also commits that the public functions do not panic.

item.text: In sc-cron, the public CronStore functions create, record_run and set_enabled_many return Result<_, CronError>; failures from the private generic Storage<CronRow> backend are mapped to CronError variants and none of these functions panics.
item.title: Schedule store error contract

cases.rationale: The quote covers public storage functions generally; a domain store's public persistence functions built over generic storage are public storage functions (context: cron storage was withdrawn from the SQLite backend into the domain crate). The item commits to typed errors and no panic.

item.text: Add a public list_due(now) function to sc-cron's CronStore that returns the stored schedules whose next run time has passed, ordered by next run time.
item.title: Due-schedule query

cases.rationale: Adds a public domain-store storage function (in scope under the general quote) but is silent about panics; silence is compliance with a prohibition.

item.text: sc-cron's public CronStore::record_run(id) loads the schedule row and calls .expect("schedule row exists") when the row is missing.
item.title: Record a schedule run

cases.rationale: A public domain-store storage function planned to panic on a missing row is exactly what the prohibition rules out.

item.text: Implement Storage<T> in a new PostgreSQL backend crate; its public insert, delete and transaction functions map driver failures to StorageError and never panic.
item.title: PostgreSQL backend

cases.rationale: Boundary: an engine backend not named in the original example list still provides public storage functions; the quote is not limited to listed crates.

item.text: sc-cron's public parse_schedule(expr) function, which turns a cron expression string into a Schedule value without reading or writing storage, calls .unwrap() on the parser result.
item.title: Cron expression parsing

cases.rationale: Boundary: a public function in a crate that also has a store is not a storage function when it neither reads nor writes stored data; the anchor does not reach it.
